name: io.swapeazi/swapeazi
title: SwapEazi
description: AI payout infrastructure for emerging markets: routes, real cost, landing time, payee safety.

tools.name: swapeazi_beneficiary_check
tools.description: Structural check on a payment destination: an IBAN's own checksum (ISO 7064 MOD 97-10), a US ABA routing number's own checksum, a BIC's format (ISO 9362), an EVM address's EIP-55 checksum, a South African universal branch code recognised against known major banks, or a SADC mobile-money number (South Africa, Zimbabwe, Malawi, Zambia) assessed for the right country code and length. Catches a mistyped or mis-keyed identifier, the single most common cause of a misdirected payment. A payment platform is several rails at once (SEPA, Fedwire/ACH, stablecoin); this assessments whichever identifiers you supply. UK sort codes and most domestic account numbers carry no public checksum and are not covered. This is NOT confirmation of payee or verification of payee: it does not confirm the name on the account, only that the identifier is internally consistent (or, for a branch code or phone number, plausible). Paid: configure this server with an Authorization Bearer key (https://swapeazi.io/pricing).

usRoutingNumber.description: A US ABA routing number, 9 digits.

saBranchCode.description: A South African universal branch code, 6 digits.

mxClabe.description: A Mexican CLABE (SPEI account), 18 digits; its verification digit is verified.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the mobile-money number: ZA, ZW, MW or ZM.

address.description: An EVM address, '0x' followed by 40 hex characters.

tools.name: get_rate_receipt
tools.description: Return a stored Rate Receipt by id (rr_...). Schema swapeazi.rate_receipt.v1. Includes max_age_seconds. Free callers see a masked publisher; a router key sees the source name.

access_key.description: A router key (rk_...), if not sent as a Bearer header.

tools.name: get_corridor_capacity
tools.description: Which banks, fintechs, stablecoin platforms and crypto P2P routes can carry one payment, e.g. 'Pay EUR 100k to Botswana', each measured the same way: corridor served (or one leg only), can carry it (yes / no / not established, against a published per-payment limit or measured P2P depth, with the source), licence in the sending and receiving country with the register, cost against the official rate (Rate Receipt where priced; otherwise 'listed, not priced', never estimated), stated speed, on/off-ramp and stablecoin path, and the forms of money each takes (bank deposit, tokenised deposit, USDC, USDT, EURC, PYUSD...) with the chains where published and whether it cashes out in the destination currency. Public sources only, every fact with its source URL and date; routes ranked by evidence of what landed (landing receipts, then verified business submissions, then public reports, each labelled), not enough evidence yet where it is thin, with landing time and delay risk next to cost; a listing never changes rank. Paid per call: x402 (USDC on Base, price in the 402 body, USD 0.25) via params._meta["x402/payment"], or a paid router key as Bearer. The free top line is GET https://swapeazi.io/api/v1/capacity. Who does what: the agent may compile the intent, gather the facts, propose the route that fits the user's own weights (recommend_payment_route) and prepare the instruction with a link to the provider's own sign-in. A person approves, releases, shares account details and authorises any spend above the mandate; the user signs in to the provider with their own credentials. SwapEazi never touches the money: it never connects a wallet and never asks for a signature.

text.description: The payment in one sentence, e.g. 'Pay EUR 100k to Botswana' or 'R500,000 from rand to Mozambique'. Or the fields below.

from.description: ISO code of the currency that leaves, e.g. EUR, USD or ZAR.

to.description: ISO code of the currency that lands, e.g. BWP, ZMW, NAD, MZN, MWK, ZAR, NGN or GHS.

amount.description: Amount that leaves, in the source currency, e.g. 100000.

access_key.description: A paid router key (rk_...), if not sent as a Bearer header.

holding.description: What the money is held as now (optional, default bank_deposit in the source currency): a bank deposit, a tokenised deposit or a named stablecoin. Each route then shows whether it takes that form directly and whether the money can be spent in the destination currency.

tools.name: plan_payment
tools.description: One call instead of five: give an amount and a corridor (e.g. amount 500, corridor EUR-XAF, payer_type business) or the payment in plain words (q). Returns the routes on record ordered by evidence of what landed ("not enough evidence yet" and no rank where it is thin), the official and street rates as separate dated fields with the all-in cost where a public price exists, the documents the sending and receiving banks are published to ask for (each with its source), and a tracking handle (plan_id): send the settlement event with it and the signed landing receipt joins the plan. Every plan carries a compliance manifest (which AML, sanctions, PSD2 and travel-rule questions it covers and which it does not) and a safety block (confidence, data freshness, sources) so another agent can decide whether to act. Signed. Free view; every route's full evidence: USD 0.25 per call by x402 in USDC on Base, or a paid key. Same plan: POST https://swapeazi.io/api/v1/plan. Information, not advice: SwapEazi is not a licensed payment provider and never sends or holds money; a person approves and the payer's own bank or provider pays.

q.description: The payment in plain words, instead of the fields, e.g. 'USD 25,000 to a supplier in Lagos'.

amount.description: The amount that leaves, in the source currency, e.g. 500.

from.description: Source currency ISO code, if not given as corridor.

to.description: Destination currency ISO code, if not given as corridor.

payer_type.description: Who pays: a business, a payout company or an individual. Default business.

payee.description: Who receives: a supplier, or people (payroll, payouts). Default from payer_type.

payout_method.description: How it should land, if it matters: bank, mobile money (e.g. MTN), cash or stablecoin.

country.description: The destination country or city, if the currency is shared (e.g. Cameroon for XAF).

access_key.description: A paid key (rk_...), if not sent as a Bearer header.

tools.name: search_routes
tools.description: Ask in plain words how to land a payment, e.g. 'land 500 EUR in Douala on MTN today' or 'USD 25,000 to a supplier in Lagos'. Returns clean JSON: the payment as understood (amount, currencies, country, payout method, operator), the official rate (legal peg or central bank) and the street rate as separate dated fields, and the routes on record ordered by evidence of what landed. A route without enough landed evidence says "not enough evidence yet" and has no rank. Each route carries cost against the mid-market rate where a public price exists, landing time, delay risk, licence, limit and sources with dates; the answer is signed (verify at POST https://swapeazi.io/api/v1/attestations/verify). Free view without a key; every route's full evidence: USD 0.25 per call by x402 in USDC on Base, or a paid key. The same search is GET https://swapeazi.io/api/v1/search?q=... Information, not advice: SwapEazi never sends or holds money; the payer's own bank or provider does.

q.description: The payment in plain words: amount, currency, where it lands, and how (bank, mobile money, cash, stablecoin) if it matters.

access_key.description: A paid key (rk_...), if not sent as a Bearer header.

tools.name: request_payment_approval
tools.description: For a payment run: the payments awaiting approval with amount, route, assessment and approval_digest, the approver role, and the payments not ready with their lifecycle state and reason. Never approves: a named person approves with approve_payment_run.

access_key.description: The router key that made the run.

tools.name: track_payment_settlement
tools.description: Spec v1.0 name for payment_run_status: each payment's lifecycle state (CREATED, ANALYSED, QUOTED, ROUTE_SELECTED, AWAITING_APPROVAL, APPROVED, SUBMITTED, PROCESSING, SETTLED, FAILED, REJECTED, EXPIRED, CANCELLED, REQUIRES_REVIEW) with the reason. SETTLED only on the provider's own confirmation.

access_key.description: The router key that made the run.

tools.name: corridor_cost
tools.description: Read-only corridor evidence: public published rates, public posts, on-chain pool prints and user receipts, summarised by corridor and provider type (bank, fintech, card, stablecoin). The free answer is the summary: how many rows, the median markup percent, the date range and the evidence label (published, user receipt, public post, on-chain, user-submitted). Row-level sources are not in the free answer. They are at GET https://swapeazi.io/api/v1/corridor-evidence/rows with a paid key or x402. Does not hold or move money. A record, not a ranking.

corridor.description: Currency pair as published, for example 'EUR/ZAR' or 'EUR-ZAR'.

pair.description: Same as corridor: two currency codes, for example 'EUR/XAF' or 'EUR-ZAR'.

from.description: ISO code of the currency sent, with to. For example EUR.

to.description: ISO code of the currency received, with from. For example ZAR.

provider_type.description: bank, fintech, card or stablecoin. Omit for every type.

detail.description: summary (the default) or full. Full rows need a paid key.
